Messages.Author: Tom Kassel
Messages.Body:
If a Bum's Rush action is intercepted and combat takes place, is the
Bum's Rush card replaced immediately? In other words, the do not
replace restriction no longer applies because it referred to a
different combat.

If the Bum's Rush initiates combat with a block and Psyche! is played
at the end of combat to start another combat, is the Bum's Rush card
replaced immediately or do you wait until the new combat is completed?

Sent via Deja.com http://www.deja.com/
Before you buy.

Messages.Author: LSJ
Messages.Body:
Tom Kassel <tka...@my-deja.com> wrote:
> If a Bum's Rush action is intercepted and combat takes place, is the
> Bum's Rush card replaced immediately? In other words, the do not
> replace restriction no longer applies because it referred to a
> different combat.

No. See Arson.

> If the Bum's Rush initiates combat with a block and Psyche! is played
> at the end of combat to start another combat, is the Bum's Rush card
> replaced immediately or do you wait until the new combat is completed?

Under the Sabbat War card text, the Bum's Rush is not replaced until
the end of the action.

OK, I'll rephrase the question. Lucky Blow, a "Do not replace until
after combat" card, is played during combat. At the end of combat,
Psyche! is played to start a new combat. Is the Lucky Blow replaced
now (after the initial combat) or after the new combat?

Assume Psyche! or other effect isn't played and all do not replace
cards are replaced. Can a newly drawn Psyche! be played? I would
assume not as we have already reached the "after combat" stage which is
later than "at the end of combat".

Tom

> assume not as we have already reached the "after combat" stage which

Psyche! - Combat (cel)
* The superior is played after combat ends, even though the card
is a combat card. [RTR 19980928]

But a newly drawn Telepathic Tracking (which is played inside of
combat) could not be played.
